fee_schedule.role_assumption: Taker (this design always buys the favored side at the ask, per AMENDMENT-20260721-H0007-pre-execution.md Sec 8). The general (non-maker) formula and M=1 apply; maker fees are not relevant to this design and would compute to $0 for weather markets regardless (default maker multiplier M=0, page 2 of the source document).
fee_schedule.formula: fees = round_up(M x 0.07 x C x P x (1-P)) dollars, where P = price in dollars, C = contract count, M = 1 (general/taker, weather-market default). Verbatim from the source document's General Trading Fees Table, page 2.
fee_schedule.rounding_rule: VERIFIED by direct cross-check against the source document's own 42-value worked-example table (pages 4-5): ceil(raw formula output) to the nearest whole cent reproduces every published value exactly. This is consistent with, and a confirmed single-fill simplification of, the more granular $0.0001-then-floor-to-account-precision mechanism docs.kalshi.com/getting_started/fee_rounding describes for multi-fill orders.
fee_schedule.min_max_fee_behavior: None found beyond the 1-cent floor implicit in the ceiling rule (e.g. price=$0.01, 1 contract -> fee=$0.01, not $0.00) -- confirmed absent, not merely unresearched.
fee_schedule.price_unit_convention: dollars in the formula (P, fee); cents at the API's public price fields and this project's stored candle columns (*_cents) -- contract_fee_cents accepts price_cents and returns whole cents.
fee_schedule.contract_count_convention: C = number of contracts in a single fill; no separate convention beyond the formula's own C term was found or needed for H0007's unit-stake (C=1) design.
fee_schedule.constant: 0.07 (general/taker formula coefficient; verified, not the earlier-flagged possibly-stale third-party figure -- see AMENDMENT-20260721-H0007-fee-verified.md Sec 1 for why this document is trusted despite that earlier caution)
